item.title: Trump says Iran ceasefire extension 'highly unlikely' as deadline looms
item.description: A two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran is set to expire Wednesday evening, with President Donald Trump declaring it "highly unlikely" he will extend the truce, raising the prospect of a return to hostilities as diplomatic efforts scramble to avert further escalation.

item.title: South Korean researchers build 'gas battery' that turns pollution into power
item.description: Researchers at Sungkyunkwan University in South Korea have developed a novel device they call a "gas battery" that captures greenhouse gases from the atmosphere and simultaneously converts them into electricity — a concept that could reshape how the world thinks about carbon capture.

item.title: Dutch intelligence warns Chinese cyberattacks on West will intensify
item.description:
The Dutch military intelligence agency MIVD on Tuesday released its annual report for 2025, warning that the risk of Chinese cyberattacks targeting Western governments and defense industries is growing and expected to intensify further this year.

MIVD Director Peter Reesink used the report's release to issue a broader call for European self-reliance in security, saying the rules-based international order that the continent has depended on for decades is under strain. "It is precisely in this space, where rules blur and power becomes more decisive, that threats grow," Reesink said. "Europe must increasingly take responsibility for its own security."

item.title: NATO revives Cold War-era sub hunting as Russia pushes into Arctic
item.description: As global attention remains fixed on the conflict in the Middle East, a quieter but consequential confrontation is unfolding beneath the waves of the Arctic and North Atlantic. Bloomberg reported on April 21 that NATO is locked in a Cold War-style undersea standoff with Russia, whose advanced nuclear submarines are pushing the alliance to revamp anti-submarine warfare capabilities not seen since the Soviet era.

item.title: Trump rejects cease-fire extension as Iran vows ‘no talks under threat’
item.description: Iran's chief negotiator Ali Bagheri Kani declared on Tuesday that Iran will not engage in negotiations while facing threats from Western powers, demanding a framework of mutual respect as a precondition for any diplomatic engagement. The statement, delivered during a press conference in Tehran, comes less than 48 hours before the US-Iran ceasefire is set to expire on Wednesday, April 22.

item.title: Macron pledges support for Lebanon ahead of Israel talks
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron met with Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam at the Élysée Palace on Tuesday, reaffirming France's commitment to the ceasefire in Lebanon and pledging to help strengthen Beirut's position ahead of a second round of direct talks with Israel later this week in Washington.

item.title: Vance's Pakistan trip delayed as Iran ceasefire nears expiration
item.description:
Vice President JD Vance did not depart Washington for Pakistan on Tuesday as planned, throwing a second round of U.S.-Iran peace talks into doubt just two days before a fragile ceasefire is set to expire.

Vance was expected to leave Tuesday morning for Islamabad to lead the American delegation in negotiations aimed at ending the conflict with Iran, which began in late February. Instead, he remained at the White House for policy meetings, according to CNN's Alayna Treene. It remains unclear whether the trip will happen at all.

item.title: Trump calls seized Iran-bound ship cargo a 'gift from China'
item.description: President Donald Trump on Tuesday described the cargo aboard an Iranian-flagged ship seized by U.S. forces as a "gift from China" to Iran, injecting a new source of friction into the U.S.-China relationship less than a month before a planned presidential summit in Beijing. The comment came as the fragile U.S.-Iran ceasefire nears expiration and investigators continue to examine thousands of containers aboard the vessel.

item.title: CATL unveils EV battery with 621-mile range, sub-7-minute charge
item.description:
CATL on Tuesday launched a suite of battery technologies at its Super Technology Day in Beijing, headlined by a third-generation Qilin battery delivering a 1,000-kilometer (621-mile) driving range and a third-generation Shenxing battery that charges from 10% to 98% in under seven minutes.

The announcements position the world's largest EV battery maker to extend its market dominance ahead of the Beijing Auto Show, which opens Friday.

item.title: Vance trip to Islamabad on hold as Iran ceasefire deadline looms
item.description: Diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran war hit a wall on Tuesday as Vice President JD Vance's planned trip to Islamabad was put on hold and Tehran sent mixed signals about whether it would join a second round of peace talks, raising fears that the fragile two-week ceasefire could collapse without a deal.

item.title: Iran calls US port blockade an 'act of war' as ceasefire set to expire Wednesday
item.description: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi declared on Tuesday that the US naval blockade of Iranian ports constitutes an "act of war" and a violation of the fragile ceasefire between Washington and Tehran, as the two-week truce enters its final hours with no extension in sight and the prospect of resumed bombing looming over the region.

item.title: Trump extends Iran ceasefire at Pakistan's request
item.description:
President Donald Trump announced Tuesday that the United States would extend its ceasefire with Iran indefinitely, reversing course just hours before the two-week truce was set to expire and after repeatedly saying an extension was "highly unlikely."

In a post on Truth Social, Trump cited a "seriously fractured" Iranian government and a direct appeal from Pakistan's Field Marshal Asim Munir and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif as his reasons for holding off on resuming military operations. "I have therefore directed our Military to continue the Blockade and, in all other respects, remain ready and able, and will therefore extend the Ceasefire until such time as their proposal is submitted, and discussions are concluded, one way or the other," Trump wrote.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV reaches Equatorial Guinea as Africa tour nears end
item.description: Pope Leo XIV called on young people in Cameroon to resist the temptation to migrate abroad, urging them instead to stay and work toward improving their communities, during a Mass attended by more than 120,000 people at Japoma Stadium in Douala on April 17.

item.title: Crude dips as Trump extends Iran ceasefire unilaterally
item.description: The ongoing war between the United States, Israel, and Iran has sent ripples through India's energy economy, pushing commercial LPG prices sharply higher and placing mounting pressure on the country's fuel supply chains, even as the government absorbs billions in lost revenue to keep retail petrol and diesel prices stable.

item.title: OpenAI plans $1.5B investment in PE joint venture
item.description:
OpenAI is set to commit up to $1.5 billion to a new joint venture with private equity firms as it races to embed its artificial intelligence tools across corporate America, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday.

The AI company plans to invest an initial $500 million of its own equity into the venture, internally codenamed "DeployCo," with an option to invest an additional $1 billion at a later stage. The joint venture is expected to be valued at $10 billion as part of a funding round projected to close in early May.

item.title: JWST detects water ice clouds on Jupiter-like exoplanet
item.description: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope have detected evidence of water ice clouds in the atmosphere of Epsilon Indi Ab, a massive gas giant just 12 light-years from Earth, according to findings published in the Astrophysical Journal Letters. The discovery challenges widely used exoplanet atmosphere models, most of which do not account for clouds, and marks a step forward in the techniques scientists will eventually need to characterize Earth-like worlds.

item.title: EU ambassadors set to approve €90bn loan for Ukraine
item.description: European Union ambassadors are expected to approve a long-delayed €90 billion loan to Ukraine on Wednesday, removing the last financial roadblock that had threatened to leave Kyiv without funding as it fights off Russia's invasion. The vote at the Committee of Permanent Representatives in Brussels comes just ten days after Viktor Orban's historic election defeat in Hungary ended his 16-year grip on power and, with it, Budapest's blockade of the aid package.

item.title: Google Cloud opens Next 2026 with major Gemini Enterprise push
item.description: Google Cloud opened its annual Next conference in Las Vegas on Wednesday with a sweeping set of announcements centered on Gemini Enterprise, the company's agentic AI platform, while deepening partnerships with consulting giants Accenture and BCG to accelerate adoption across global enterprises.

item.title: Iran seizes two ships, fires on third in Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps opened fire on three commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, seizing two and leaving a third stranded along the Iranian coast, in a sharp escalation that came just hours after President Trump announced he was indefinitely extending a ceasefire with Tehran.

The IRGC captured the Panama-flagged MSC Francesca and the Liberia-flagged Epaminondas, both container ships, and directed them to Iranian waters, according to a statement carried by AFP. A third vessel, the Greek-owned Euphoria, was also targeted and is now stranded off the Iranian coast, according to semiofficial Iranian news agency Fars. The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency reported that the first ship was "assaulted by a gunboat" from the IRGC at approximately 7:55 a.m. local time.

The IRGC claimed the vessels "allegedly operated without authorization, repeatedly violated regulations, manipulated navigational aid systems and sought to covertly exit the Strait of Hormuz, endangering maritime security". The statement added that "disruption of order and safety in the Strait of Hormuz is our red line".

item.title: Trump claims Iran 'collapsing financially' amid US naval blockade
item.description: President Donald Trump declared on Tuesday that Iran is "collapsing financially" and losing $500 million a day, escalating his rhetoric as a fragile ceasefire teeters and diplomatic efforts to end the nearly two-month-old conflict stall.
